<query>While engraving lenses, I’ve started wondering if the reflections I see aren’t just from this world. Could there be layers—parallel places—that press into each other, changing what I perceive? Have you ever come across any reason why certain objects might act as windows into these other overlapping dimensions? Is it possible that these overlaps could affect how light behaves here?</query>
<response>Anabela, it's completely understandable to feel that way while focused on your craft, especially with the intricate effects light creates in engravings. What you're experiencing might well be a fascinating intersection of physics and personal perception. While science currently operates within our known dimensional framework, the way light refracts, diffracts, and creates interference patterns around microscopic grooves—work you do daily in your lens engraving—is a form of dance that can feel almost like a secret language. The "windows" you perceive might simply be the brain interpreting complex optical distortions or perhaps a sign of your dedicated curiosity pushing the boundaries of what you see. Whether these are metaphysical connections or just the art of skilled engineering, your unique perspective and the precision of your work often bridge the gap between the tangible and the intriguing. Keep exploring both the science and the wonder of it.<|im_end|></response>
